long_description.before: Firecrawl is the web context API for AI agents. Search, scrape, parse, and interact with the live web to turn any source into clean Markdown or structured data your agents can ship with. Open source, ZDR-ready, and trusted by 80,000+ teams including Apple, Shopify, Canva, Zapier, and Lovable to power production AI.
long_description.after:
Firecrawl is the easiest way to turn the web into data AI agents can use. One API call converts any URL into clean, LLM-ready markdown or structured data - the boring-hard problem everyone building with LLMs eventually hits, solved.

We hit 8 figures in ARR in year one and more than doubled it in year two. We have 150k+ GitHub stars, and developers, agents, and category-defining AI companies build on us every day. Growth like this is rare, and we're just getting started.

We're a small team punching far above our weight. Everyone here owns a real piece of the product and company, end to end, and runs it themselves - no hiding behind process or headcount.

This is a place for people who want to work at the frontier: an AI company building the infrastructure other AI companies run on, not one bolting AI onto an existing product. We move fast, go deep, and are building the tools superintelligence will rely on to gather data from the web.

long_description.before:
Promi is an AI-powered price and discount optimization platform. We help eCommerce merchants personalize their sales to generate additional revenue and profit.

Ecommerce merchants and marketers typically use discounts to drive customer acquisition, boost sales during holidays, or liquidate inventory. But deciding on a discount to offer is typically guesswork. Who to send the discount to, how much to offer, and which products it applies to are, in the most advanced cases, determined manually by looking at past sales and seeing what worked well. In the majority of cases, it's what feels and sounds good.

Promi leverages store data to optimize discounts at a more granular level than possible manually. We dynamically determine the best value across each product, for different users, at different times in order to maximize sales and profit.
long_description.after:
Promi provides product feedback in the form of customer interviews, URL walkthroughs, heatmaps, and more by creating digital twins of your existing customers. We ingest data from Posthog, Intercom, Stripe, etc. to create your personas from real product usage data. By factoring in how your customers actually interact with product features, we provide much more relevant and insightful feedback on what you are building.

We aren't trying to replace user research, but in our experiences most products don't have the time or budget to talk to real users. Getting synthetic feedback is the next best thing, and can/should be a part of launching any products.

one_liner.before: Optimizing ecommerce pricing with dynamic, personalized discounts
one_liner.after: Providing quick product and design feedback via digital twins

long_description.after:
Control Seat builds the hardware and software that helps industrial teams see, understand, and run their operations.

Our platform creates one clear source of truth across the plant. It connects the systems teams already use, brings control, monitoring, history, and machine health together, and adds an intelligence layer that continuously watches for meaningful changes. Teams can understand what happened, catch problems earlier, and act before they become downtime.

The result is fewer surprises, faster decisions, and less time spent piecing together information across disconnected tools.

We work with manufacturers, utilities, energy companies, and other industrial operators modernizing existing facilities or building new ones.

long_description.before: We manufacture humanoid robots in San Francisco.
long_description.after:
Nori builds home robots that cost less than $2,000 and that anyone can teach. Out of the box, the NORI L3 does household chores: loading the dishwasher, folding laundry, tidying up. But because anyone can train it, it also learns your specific tasks, like washing paintbrushes if you're an artist or flipping sheet music while you play guitar. It's a general-purpose robot, not an appliance.

We launched pre-orders 6 weeks ago and have already booked $100K in revenue.

Humanoid robots exist, but they cost $20,000 or more and are demoed, not shipped. We got to $1,688 without sacrificing capability. Instead of expensive actuators, we use low-cost servos and get more out of them through smarter control and design. A wheeled base with a lift gives full floor-to-counter reach without the cost and fragility of legs, and we streamlined manufacturing from day one, assembling in the US.

The teachability is the moat. Every skill a user trains can be shared, so each customer makes every robot more capable. Hardware is the entry point; the skill ecosystem is the recurring revenue.

We're robotics researchers from Columbia labs like RoboPIL (robot learning) and CGUI. Working with $100K research robots that struggled with everyday tasks convinced us the problem isn't capability, it's cost. Good robots don't need to be expensive.

Households already spend $2,000+ on single-task machines: a dishwasher, a washing machine, a vacuum. We sell one robot at $1,688 that does the work of all of them and learns more. At 5% of US households and $25 a month for skills, that's $2B a year in recurring revenue, on top of hardware.

one_liner.before: Sub-2000$ robotic humanoid assembled in the US
one_liner.after: Affordable robot you can teach to do anything

long_description.after:
The technologies that define this century, including data centers, rockets, satellites, and robots, are built from complex metal parts. As these systems advance, the parts get harder to make. Past a certain complexity, casting and machining stop working, and the advanced methods that remain are slow, expensive, and hazardous.

Ultrasonium has invented a new manufacturing method to make these critical parts 15x faster and 75% cheaper than the methods they replace, in the U.S. and at scale. Solid metal feedstock goes in and a finished part safely comes out, controlled by a physical AI layer and novel control processes. 

The systems that matter most, in aerospace, energy, and compute, are demanding metal geometries that can't be machined or cast and are too expensive and slow to make with incumbent methods, at a moment when domestic manufacturing capacity is a national priority.

Our founding team has built and innovated some of the most complex engineering systems known to man: quantum computers, superconductors, nuclear reactors, and novel aerospace alloy processing methods.

long_description.before:
Osseus is the intelligent design platform for robotics. Today, it gives robotics teams a collaborative web app for reviewing mechanical and electrical designs against the full context around them. Engineers and suppliers comment on the exact part, net, connector, or dimension, while AI AutoReview compares proposed changes with prior revisions and source evidence.

Underneath is a secure research brain that connects physical designs, robot descriptions and models, firmware and robot software, simulation and test results, supplier feedback, decisions, and owners in one permissioned, version-aware record. Because Osseus understands those relationships, it can carry supplier constraints into future reviews, trace a hardware change into the exact configurations, code, and validation work it affects, and turn approved findings into owned work without losing the evidence or rationale.

Our long-term goal is for any professional team or hobbyist to import, fork, or create a robot in Osseus. Builders will be able to explore compatible components and supplier intelligence, edit the physical design, and receive proposed updates to the robot description, firmware, control software, simulation, and tests. We ultimately want to develop physical-AI models that reason jointly over the robot's geometry, electronics, kinematics, components, software, and real-world performance so people can optimize and iterate on robots much faster.
